newsitem.title: UK: Still in holiday mode, Bradys make sleepy '97 start.
newsitem.headline: Still in holiday mode, Bradys make sleepy '97 start.

text.p: The Brady debt market eased into the first trading day of 1997 with prices softening across the board after the New Year's Eve fall in U.S. Treasuries, but traders were hoping for a boost once New York clocks in.
With Russian players out until the middle of next week due to the January 7 Orthodox Christmas, and Europe readying for the Epiphany holiday on Monday, the Brady market was not yet in full stream.
What action there was centred on Russian loans and a handful of Latin credits, but traders said that activity was mainly due to short covering.
"The market is not that depressed, but it has lost its buying momentum for the time being -- we are waiting for New York to come in," said one dealer at a U.S. firm here.
The U.S. long bond fell more than a point before stabilising to yield 6.644 after data released on New Year's Eve showed strength in U.S. home sales and a rise in consumer confidence.

The fall soured the end of an otherwise bumper year for the emerging debt market. WestMerchant Capital Markets said the WestMerchant Price Index (WMBI) showed a rise of 33.3 percent over the course of 1996, compared with 14.4 percent in 1995.
The average stripped spread of all the performing assets in the index almost halved to 529 basis points over Treasuries, compared with 1,048 b.p. at the end of 1995, the bank said.
Russian dollar Vnesh loans eased slightly in early trading but later recovered some of the lost ground. They were quoted down 1/4 at 79-3/8 at 1145 GMT.
Traders also reported some action in Brazilian C bonds and Argentine FRBs.
"A few clients went into Christmas a bit short -- what we're seeing today looks like a short covering-made bump," the dealer said.
Brazilian C's and FRBs both shed 1/8, slipping to 73-1/2 and 86-7/8 respectively.
Bulgaria, adrift without a prime minister for more than a week, drifted lower in line with the market's softer tone, but traders reported little trading there.
IABs were quoted down 1/2 at 50-5/8. --Caroline Brothers, London Newsroom +44 171 542 2734
